newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss stocks end firmer on late boost.
newsitem.headline: Swiss stocks end firmer on late boost.

text.p: Swiss shares recovered from intra-day lows to end firmer, closing above an important resistance mark around 3,760/70 points on the Swiss Market Index (SMI) of leading shares.
Dealers said it was crucial for the SMI to end above 3,770 points to clear the way for further advances. One trader added U.S. August factory orders triggered buying.
The SMI closed higher by 11.4 points, or 0.3 percent, at 3,771.6 points.
The all-share Swiss Performance Index (SPI) added 8.02 points, or 0.33 percent, to 2,415.18.
One dealer said prospects for a continued strong performance were favourable.
"Things look good thanks to the positive interest rate environment and renewed demand", he noted, adding that volumes were below those of yesterday.
Heavily-traded Roche certificats were sought throughout the session, ending 0.91 percent higher at 9,460 francs. Ciba and Sandoz closed marginally stronger.
Among major financials, CS Holding stood out with a gain of 1.2 percent to 126.75 francs. Swiss Re fell one franc to 1,332.
Nestle gave up three francs to 1,395.

The stocks of technology concern Sulzer ended up four francs at 749, well below an intra-day high at 762. One dealer said technical factors and the settlement of a U.S. patent infringement suit were reasons for the stong bias during the day.
Swissair, recently under pressure, added two percent to 1,069 francs.
Second-tier Sika and Fischer saw gains of two percent.
